newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy banks profitable but future uncertain - study.
newsitem.headline: Italy banks profitable but future uncertain - study.

text.p: Italian banks can expect to see net profit of some 6.9 trillion lire this year and above 7.4 trillion in 1997 but the fragility of the banking system is set to increase, private research body Prometeia said.
Margin spreads will become even tighter and there will be less gains from brokerage services, Prometeia said in a study.

The increase in net profit, benefiting from lower provisions and credit adjustments, is however "completely insufficient to bring a return on assets to acceptable levels consistent with market rates and with an adequate risk premium," it said.
This rise in net profit contrasts with the trend in operating profits, forecast to rise 23.9 percent this year, but seen falling 8.0 percent in 1997 and 7.0 percent in 1988.

Strongly limited interest margins are seen eroding operating profits although they will continue to account for 70 percent of earning margins, although decreasing in 1997. This will be only in part compensated by an increase in revenues from services and trading profits and by lower labour costs, Prometeia said.
